newsitem.title: USA: S&P says maintains Aa rating on Los Angeles debt.
newsitem.headline: S&P says maintains Aa rating on Los Angeles debt.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp on Monday said it would maintain its Aa rating on the general obligation bonds of the city of Los Angeles despite the passage of a tax measure that could hurt city revenues.
"We think that the flexibility that they have now is represented by our Aa (bond rating)," said Chris Irwin, an S&P director. "We don't expect any near-term credit impact (from Proposition 218)."
Proposition 218, approved in November, amended the state Constitution to require voter approval of most tax or fee increases and curtailed the use of many types of assessments.
"We do review the city every year and maintenance of the ratings in the future is going to depend on their ability to maintain their current financial position."
Moody's Investors Service Inc on Friday said it reviewed and lowered the rating on the city's general obligation bonds to Aa from Aa1.
Moody's said a primary reason for the rating downgrade was the anticipated reduction in revenue flexibility due to Proposition 218.
